justification: This article renders essentially flawlessly on the design/UX axis, and the real numbers back that up: Lighthouse 100/100/100/100, zero console errors, zero broken links (30/30 internal), zero mobile overflow. Both required figures are present and legible in all four device/theme combinations checked. Figure 1 (observer fan-out, viewBox 360x260) is a clean portrait diagram: SensorHub box at top with two arrows fanning down to ConsoleDisplay and ThresholdAlert, annotation text underneath the boxes rather than beside them, fully readable in mobile-dark and mobile-light at 390px with no faded edge and no text below the 12-unit minimum. Figure 2 (decorator chain, viewBox 360x350) is a four-box vertical stack (StreamWriter -> GZipStream -> CountingStream -> MemoryStream) with the CountingStream box correctly highlighted in the accent color to mark 'ours' versus the three BCL types; same clean rendering in both themes on mobile, and on desktop (desktop-dark-part08, desktop-light-part09) it sits as a centered, appropriately-sized column rather than stretching or looking like an abandoned island. Code blocks behave exactly as the writer guide predicts for mobile: long lines (constructor calls, WriteLine format strings, class headers with generic constraints) fade at the ~40-column boundary while the operative tokens the prose is discussing stay on-screen before the fade, and desktop renders every line in full with no wrapping artifacts. All four exercises were checked against the predict-the-output leak rule and none violate it. Exercise 1 ('Explain the tie') is pure prose, no code or output in the question. Exercise 2 ('Add a self-unsubscribing observer') is extend-the-code: the question describes the requirement in prose only, and the full LimitedObserver<T> implementation plus its text output block live entirely inside the collapsed :::solution, confirmed collapsed by default in both mobile-dark-part10 and mobile-light-part10 screenshots. Exercise 4 ('Name the pattern already doing the work') is conceptual prose with no code. Exercise 3 ('Explain the exception') is the one this round was asked to scrutinize specifically: its question shows a `csharp run throws=ObjectDisposedException` code block with the red 'Throws ObjectDisposedException' badge visible above the code, and no `text output` block follows it -- confirmed in both mobile-dark-part13 and mobile-light-part14. This is not a predicted-output leak, because a throws= badge states only the exception type (the category of failure), not the reasoning that is the actual thing being tested (which constructor argument is missing and why disposal cascades to a stream GZipStream never subclasses) -- that reasoning is withheld in :::solution. This is the same shape as the established `error=CS0315` precedent in interfaces-vs-abstract-classes.md's 'Why does this not compile?' exercise (line 523-524 of that article), which shows the red 'Does not compile: CS0315' label directly in the question with no further detail, and asks the reader to supply the reasoning in prose before opening the solution. The two conventions are directly analogous (a compile-time red label there, a runtime red label here), so this is correctly applying precedent, not a violation. Two nearly-invisible nitpicks keep this out of a perfect score: on desktop the decorator figure column ends up noticeably narrower than the text column it sits in (an inherent consequence of the 360-wide viewBox rule for a diagram this simple, not a defect), and this article's per-code-block mobile clipping is slightly heavier than average for the site because several of its programs are four-class multi-type listings (PriceFeed/PriceChangedEventArgs, SensorHub/ConsoleDisplay/ThresholdAlert/Unsubscriber, CountingStream) that run long even before hitting the fade boundary -- legible throughout, just busier scrolling than a shorter listing would be.
